attendance at a hospital antenatal clinic
Birthing location (Wellington Hospital vs. primary unit)
outcome: Compliance with Routine Antenatal Anti-D Prophylaxis (RAADP) guidelines
cohort: Rhesus-negative individuals who gave birth in Wellington, New Zealand, maternity units over a 6-month period
finding: Compliance with Routine Antenatal Anti-D Prophylaxis (RAADP) guidelines is suboptimal and influenced by factors such as type of obstetrician care, proximity to the hospital, and birthing location, indicating inequitable access to care.
mod_finding: Mode of birth did not influence the likelihood of receiving RAADP.
